messages:
Nina: heads-up — nightly perf dashboard triggered a p95 latency alert on /generate (us-west-2). +120% vs baseline around 00:30 UTC.
Sam: saw that, thanks. any correlated deploys or rollouts? :thinking_face:
deploy-bot: canary deploy pr/5123 -> prod/us-west-2 at 6709123400 (user: Leo)
Leo: that canary touched the prefetch/batcher config and bumped `default_coalesce_ms` from 6 -> 12 in kernel-affinity branch.
Mia: interesting — the metric looks like KV cache miss amplification: p95 jumps while throughput steady, suggests tail inflation not load.
Nina: perf-bot traces show a hot sweep event in kv-evict where many shards scanned after the config change. snippet from logs:
```
kv_eviction: scanned_shards=48 prefetch_hits=12 prefetch_misses=184 sweep_duration_ms=420
kernel_selector: selected_kernel=polymorphic_v2 batch_size=1
```
Sam: can we repro locally against the same commit? I'd like to run the microbench used by CI: `./ci/run_perf.sh --suite=nightly/kv-hot-sweep --region=us-west-2`
Leo: running now. also starting a `git bisect` between main~6 and pr/5123 to confirm causality.
perf-bot: ci/nightly-run-eviction failed on commit 9f3d2b1 (pr/5123) — p95 regression +95% (compare baseline 6709040000)
Mia: quick mitigation: rolling back the `default_coalesce_ms` change in canary would avoid the sweep amplification while we dig in.
Nina: +1 for rollback if canary is impacting dedicated pools. ops, can we pause rollout? @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for pr/5123 canary in prod/us-west-2 at 6709123589 — status: in-progress
Sam: after rollback, let's collect heap/proc stats and a kernel selection dump (use `--dump-kernel-map`) at 1:1 sampling for 2 minutes.
Leo: confirmed: rollback decreased p95 within one window. keeping canary paused. I'll open a follow-up PR to change the eviction window and add unit test for sweep bounds.
Mia: add perf regression test to CI (nightly-run-eviction) that asserts <10% p95 drift on small-memory hotset workloads.
Nina: filing incident note and linking this thread. we should also add an observability alert for sweep_duration_ms > 200ms per-shard. :white_check_mark:
